5.4.2 Angiotensin II type I receptor blo.summary: ARBs are recommended for patients with HFrEF who cannot tolerate ACE-I or ARNI due to side effects. Candesartan (CHARM-Alternative) reduced CV deaths and HF hospitalizations in patients not receiving an ACE-I due to intolerance. Valsartan (Val-HeFT) reduced HF hospitalizations in addition to usual therapy including ACE-I. No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial.
5.4.2 Angiotensin II type I receptor blo.notes: Use when ACE-I/ARNI not tolerated; evidence from CHARM-Alternative and Val-HeFT trials.

5.4.3 I_f-channel inhibitor (Ivabradine).summary: Ivabradine slows heart rate by inhibiting the I_f channel in the sinus node. It is effective only in patients in sinus rhythm (SR). Ivabradine reduced the combined endpoint of CV mortality and HF hospitalization in symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤35%, HF hospitalization in recent 12 months, in SR, and with resting heart rate thresholds used in trials. Recommendation based on SHIFT trial heart-rate criteria. EMA approved use in Europe for patients with HFrEF with LVEF ≤35% in SR with resting heart rate ≥75 bpm in certain subgroups.
indications: Elevated resting heart rate (trial-used thresholds e.g., ≥70 or ≥75 bpm depending on guideline/EMA)
5.4.3 I_f-channel inhibitor (Ivabradine).practical_guidance: Begin and uptitrate beta-blocker therapy to guideline-recommended/maximally tolerated doses before considering ivabradine. See Supplementary Table 8 for dosing guidance.
evidence_notes: Primary recommendation based on SHIFT trial
EMA approval based on retrospective subgroup analysis showing survival benefit in specific heart-rate subgroup

5.4.4 Combination of hydralazine and iso.summary: No clear evidence to support fixed-dose combination use in all patients with HFrEF. A small RCT in self-identified black patients showed addition of hydralazine+isosorbide dinitrate to conventional therapy reduced mortality and HF hospitalizations (NYHA III–IV). Results may not translate to other racial/ethnic groups.
indications: Consider in symptomatic HFrEF patients who cannot tolerate ACE-I, ARNI, or ARB (or if contraindicated) to reduce mortality
Evidence largely from a small Veterans Administration Cooperative Study (mostly male patients) and a trial in self-identified black patients
5.4.4 Combination of hydralazine and iso.notes: Recommendation based on relatively small trials with limited generalizability.

5.4.5 Digoxin.summary: Digoxin may be considered in patients with HFrEF in sinus rhythm to reduce risk of hospitalization, though overall effect on mortality was neutral in DIG trial. Effects in patients with HFrEF and AF not well-studied in RCTs; some studies suggest higher risk with AF, others indicate no deleterious effect on mortality. Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic window; aim for serum concentration <1.2 ng/mL. Exercise caution in females, elderly, frail, hypokalaemic patients.
indications: Symptomatic HFrEF in sinus rhythm to reduce hospitalization risk
May be useful in HFrEF with AF and rapid ventricular rate when other options cannot be used (based on non-RCT data)
safety: Use caution in females, elderly, frail, hypokalaemic patients
evidence_notes: DIG trial: neutral effect on mortality
Conflicting observational/meta-analysis data for patients with AF

general_terms_and_abbreviations_on_page: HFrEF (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction)
content.references_mentioned: Numerous trial references cited (e.g., CHARM-Alternative, Val-HeFT, SHIFT, DIG) and numbered citations present on the page.
